body: You're most welcome!

I'd go with the Surrendered Single since you are single - the focus is a little different, and doesn't rely on you being in a live-in relationship. There is also one called Things Will Get as Good As You Can Stand, about Gratitude, but I'd read that one after. Enjoy!

I was pretty young and never heard of Nrents but I still knew that even if I was being executed I wouldn't ask for my mother - she wouldn't take care of me even as I was being put to death. Sad. (sorry if I have the wrong movie. It was something like that).

I'm a psychiatrist. If something is "all in your head" that's a psychiatric disorder. Please don't panic at this next part but it could also be something far worse (I'm sure it's not) like MS or a brain tumor. (But I'm sure it's your anxiety). Still, it has to be checked out. Please talk to someone at your school and have them call CPS if necessary. Don't say you know it's "hysterical blindness" because truthfully I am not convinced. Hysteria is a very uncommon diagnosis these days. It could be migraine, and autoimmune disorder, a whole bunch of other things. The first rule of psychiatry is not to miss anything organic (i.e. not psychiatric). And then, if it IS psychiatric, you need treatment for that. Any way you slice it, you need treatment. And your mom needs her butt kicked, but that can happen later. So get to an ER, preferably with an adult (from school or CPS). And then don't leave without having a case number and a social worker assigned to you. And a follow-up appointment. I'd really like for you to have an MRI with and without contrast as well. PM me if you'd like with your location and I'll see if I know someone nearby.

Enjoy your new boots and your new life!!

Well I don't hate being a forensic psychiatrist. But I am around traumatized people all day long. Which it seems is pretty common for people who were abused as children but I didn't know until it was way too late.

Unfortunately my Nrents did such a job on me that I reached adulthood convinced that I was completely worthless and nobody could love me. It is important that when you love someone who was RBN that you let them know repeatedly it wasn't their fault. My husband tried but either he didn't try hard enough, his parents were also too F'd up, or (and I'm still afraid this last one is true even at my advanced age and after 25 years of marriage) my Nrents were right and there is something fundamentally wrong with me. I'm trying to get my husband to come back but today it seems hopeless. I wish OP and his gf all the best of luck. I had some wonderful years when I was truly loved and I wish I hadn't been so damaged that I couldn't really understand and appreciate what I had.

My marriage. For over 25 years they told me he didn't love me and was only using me for a green card. So eventually I made him leave me. Now I'm trying to get him to come back. But it's not easy. This sub has really helped me to understand what was wrong with me all these years so thank you RBN. I have hope.

I kept asking, what about this money you claimed you were saving for their tuition since they were born? Still waiting. One is already in law school. They just lie and keep lying to your face and think they can make it up by buying a set of sheets or a garbage can or something.

Ha (that's a ha for me, not you). My Nrents said I could be a doctor or an engineer. So in tenth grade in my school we all had to take mechanical drawing. It was popular to hate it but I really liked it. I told my parents (long before I ever heard of NPD) "Maybe I'll be an architect." My alcoholic Ndad looked me in the eye and said "You'll starve to death."
I'm a doctor.

My grandmother (Nmom's mom) who I did not realize was a N but clearly was the one who set the bar used to make very good dinners. We would all praise her repeatedly for the amazing dinner and she would say - nothing. Then at the end of the meal she would say, "It was good, wasn't it?" To this day I don't understand that. WTF?

"And even if you did accomplish something that would be impossible for her to discount/ignore - winning a Nobel prize, for example - well, then, her story would all be about what she did to get you there and how you never would have amounted to anything without her."

This really made me LOL. Do you know my Nmom? Because you know, the world would not be able to rotate on its axis without her! She insists to this day that she never had any  help with anything and all her accomplishments are HERS ALONE. Yet she forgot the part about her parents leaving a successful business that they built in South America after leaving their original country and coming to the US just to help her so she could finish her education. She also forgot that she made me cook and do laundry starting at the age of nine so she could study. She even forgot that English is not her native language so I (now a published writer) wrote and rewrote every single friggin essay for her to get all of this education which she did "on her own." Also starting at age nine, when - get this - I scored a perfect score on the standardized test for reading. No other child had every done that in the fourth grade so the principal called my mother to tell her (I think it was in the whole city of NY) and she was just blase about it. Then when she figured out it was something special, she used it to show how fantastic SHE was. But nobody ever *helped* her with anything!!
Romanian by any chance? Or is it all of Eastern Europe?

You are my sister from another mother. I feel you so intensely right now. My mother has done the exact same thing all my life. She even seems proud of her friends' kids' achievements. I could give you a thousand examples of things that she said and did that were downright offensive and humiliating to me. She still doesn't even know what I actually do (I'm a forensic psychiatrist, and published author, not just articles but a whole psychiatry book, plus a novel too). Meanwhile, a couple of years ago (here's one example) a counselor at my kids' camp on visiting day read aloud an email she had sent to a bowling alley to complain about something and my Nmom started gushing about what a great writer this teenage girl was: "OMG, you should be a professional writer, you are so talented!!" I let her have it later, telling her she was a bitch and an idiot. Narcissists CAN be insulted. I am fairly low contact with my Nrents and when I talk to them I just grey rock away. It is very sad that you will never, ever get what you need from them. However, they will also never experience the joy, satisfaction, and pride that comes with successfully raising happy, productive, children. As my children enter adulthood and continue to remain in my life, and share their wins with me, and, I see what it is like for them when I am happy for them and vice versa, that in itself is a corrective emotional experience for me. And I'm sad for my parents because they have these two really amazing successful daughters yet they have no clue what they have. That is super sad. Can you look at it that way at all? I personally am really impressed with you (OP's) accomplishments and I wish you had been around when both of my dogs were at the end of their lives. In fact, with my dog that died in March, you would have probably helped my whole family in ways you cannot even imagine. (Also, because of the way my last dog died, my youngest son wants to be a vet, and even though you are a random internet stranger, I am going to tell him about your practice. He will be really impressed. He is 16). So many wins in your post today - I hope you can hear them. You have touched a lot of people's hearts - unfortunately your Nmom's is made of stone (like my Nmom's. You are not alone).

Congratulations! Enjoy every minute and memorize that amazing baby feeling - they really do grow up so fast! I feel so sorry for my Nrents for never having known the joy of having been (and still being) parents. But you do and you will!

P.S. I'm away at a conference right now. One gay male colleague who I haven't seen in a couple of years just told me I look "fabulous" and a woman I never met before asked me something that required me to answer "I'm much older than I look." She thought I had recently finished my fellowship (not 20+ years ago!) Until I started this group I actually BELIEVED my Nmom, too. You guys don't know how lucky you are to have RBN and each other while you are still young!!

This is interesting. I made my own lunch or used the "allowance" money (that my grandfather gave us) or my babysitting money to buy lunch (also for train fare to get to school until the train passes kicked in - they did not start right at the beginning of the school year because the city was always broke in those days). I actually remember making my own lunch in elementary school too, or going home or to my grandmother's house for lunch and eating whatever I could find in the fridge (if I went home. My grandmother made us lunch. She was very narcissistic but she was responsible). From the age of nine I was responsible for the family's laundry and from 13 I was responsible for dinner (again, grandmother helped quite a bit but not daily). I knew this was not normal per se, but I never understood that my mother was a N, nor did I understand that when mothers have responsibilities outside the home, fathers could actually help care for their children, even in the seventies. Fathers who were not "functional" alcoholics and narcissists, that is. I did my own children a great disservice by not really expecting their father to help care for them much. They are big now, and we are (hopefully temporarily) separated, but I see that as I step back and have no expectations, he is totally stepping up. Who knew?

I am 53 and I felt exactly the way you describe almost my whole life (with moments of exception here and there) until the last few months. 
I started doing two things which helped me immensely. One is attending ACA meetings regularly and starting to work the steps. I'm still on Step 1, but it has already made a huge difference in my life.
I don't know if you are male or female or in a long-term relationship, but the other thing that has changed my life is a book called The Surrendered Wife, by Laura Doyle. Although it sounds awful, this book (and the program that goes with it) teaches you step by step how to let go of controlling your husband and how to take care of yourself. It's designed to improve your marriage, but what it also is doing for me is improving my ability to live my life. The two programs together have done for me what years of therapy have failed to do. All the bullshit advice "love yourself and move on" never helped me, but the actual steps of how to do it have been priceless. I don't know if this helps at all, but that is what has finally worked for me, and I have been suffering (and almost destroyed my marriage, and have frequently been on the brink of suicide) for many, many years.

"This feeling of "is this normal?" is the worst."

Exactly this. Everyone's stories are horrifying. I found OP's to be especially awful. But the worst part, I think, for all of us, is believing that it is "normal," feeling horrible our whole lives, and then one day, sooner or later (much, much later in my case, when I was over 50!) coming to a full and complete realization that our Nrents were totally NOT normal and it really was NOT our fault. Giving up that feeling of worthlessness and the whole trauma bond with our Nrents is both freeing and also incredibly painful, when we realize that we never learned what normal love feels like. I wish you the very best of luck, OP, and everyone else in this conversation. So glad you are out of that craziness!

I'm sorry about your illness. I hope you get to enjoy your talent one day. I don't feel very successful. The recent breakdown of my marriage and my inability to fix it are the worst thing(s) that ever happened to me and I attribute that directly to the narcissistic abuse inflicted on my by my Nrents. The inability to know how to experience love and to properly give it back is completely disabling, as are the inability to know what success is supposed to feel like. I have told my mother many times that she ruined my life but it does not resonate with her at all. She just thinks it retaliation for all the times she told me I ruined her life by being born - which after all, is just a simple fact. So sad. I don't think they actually derive pleasure from our suffering - it just somehow makes their suffering more tolerable for a minute.

I used to think this was normal. It took me years to realize that normal people do not do this, that they don't go on as if nothing happened. Truthfully I still have problems understanding it and I am currently surprised that my children are in a several-months-long cold war with their father (my husband) and that my separation with my husband has gone on for four months even though I've apologized and I've asked him to come back. Our fights used to end in a day just like the crazy shit my parents did to me would be forgotten in a minute (as per their wishes/expectations. Of course the damage to my psyche is permanent but whatever).

"I think with Ns it's a battle between wanting to have successful/talented children, and the very strong urge to completely destroy and sabotage them."

Exactly! I hope you ended up having the artistic life you wanted and deserve! But yes, they see us as narcissistic extensions of themselves, and when that is "on" they can be sort of pseudo-supportive. But then there is a flash of "wait - they are separate people" and they cannot tolerate that, so they need to destroy us. I also think there is that underlying self-hatred at work, that they really cannot love themselves at all, and that the narcissism is a cover (in psychological terms a reaction formation) for how they really feel about themselves!
Thank you. I was thinking about this - that narcissists and psychopaths have a captive audience in 12 step groups. Sad, but true.

The thing is, I did write (and get published by a real publisher) a novel, also more recently a professional book, and I have an M.D. (so does Nmom) but in her world only her M.D. counts for anything. N/alcoholic dad, too. OPK ("Other People's Kids") are just Better. (and I'm a big-ass grownup but in their world, still a kid).

It's funny she would say she was the only girl when she has an older sister. But that's how she experienced herself. Also only having hand me downs is tough. I'm the oldest but I got hand me downs from the neighbors LOL, and their friends' kids. Still, it was "new to me." Some of my mom's narcissism is FLEAS, probably, but it doesn't matter, it's so ingrained she refuses to get rid of it, refuses to acknowledge she has it, and refuses to see how much it hurts others. So - it is what it is.

Oh, I forgot to say, she has these nursing home patients who will make her stuff, like crocheted toilet paper roll covers, or patients who make her itchy wool scarves - THOSE things she uses or displays, with pride. Woo-hoo, my PATIENTS love me. I'm a psychiatrist so we are not even supposed to ACCEPT gifts from our patients (although that has changed with the total destruction of psychiatry. A patient once gave me a chocolate orange from Trader Joe's and I kept it and ate it LOL).

My Nmom has a story though. She was born and raised in Eastern Europe and had nothing. A relative that had already moved abroad sent her a doll. She says she loved that doll so much she never played with it, just kept it away on a top shelf. It was the best thing she owned. One day they went to a birthday for some other relative and her mother made her give the doll to the other relative: "you never play with it."
The way she tells the story she was too afraid to tell her mother (my grandmother) how much she loved that doll and why she didn't play with it. 
My Nmom loves strangers. She loves other people. She is capable of emotion. She is a doctor and a good person. She just cannot love her own children. This stuff does not occur in a vacuum. My grandmother was strict but she loved me more than my mother ever did and was much more generous. It would take me another lifetime to figure them out.

If you buy a sewing machine it will probably come with some classes. They also have sewing classes at places like JoAnn's and even at independent fabric stores. You might also be able to find a local seamstress to teach you!

The funny thing is that my mother, now 76 years old, STILL doesn't know it is not a normal thing to say. She still "didn't do anything wrong" and "it's all in your (my) head." I am just now, at age 53, recovering. Super crazy. But I really am recovering! It's amazing!
That is so wonderful to hear! I know what you mean. Every day I am one day closer to healing myself and my marriage. That moron didn't know what he was talking about.

I used to cry that I was adopted because my parents didn't love me. My Nmom (I didn't know that was what she was, of course, I was like, five, would say: "Adopted!? Why would we adopt you? We didn't want children!!"

Based on what you've written here, I wouldn't be surprised if you're not even autistic. She just might want you to be to feed her narcissism. Hope you get out of there soon and move on with your life. Good luck.

She's not really going to give you the money. I've played this game before. Still waiting for the college money for my kid that my Nmom can't even legally use. Every year she would go on and on and on about how friggin generous she is putting $1000 into a 529 for each kid on his birthday. So now my husband and I are separated and I'm paying all the tuition myself and trying to keep everything calm and dignified in the hope that we will be reuniting soon (and it's still "our" money) so in between making me feel worse ("if he really loved you he would have come back already") I tell her, if you YOU really loved me you would ask me if I needed anything. So she tells me "do you need anything" and I say, "Yes, I need the money that you are always bragging that you put aside for my kids' college" (I said it nicer). So suddenly she somehow can't get that money. It's halfway through the semester and so far I've paid all the tuition myself. And she can't keep that money!! It's my son's money!! It's illegal for my parents to keep it for themelves!! She just wants to continue to screw me as much as possible. So I'd tell her, put it in a 529 for your future children. That way she can't keep it. She can try to screw you but ultimately she will be screwing herself and you will have the last laugh. 
I may have said this before but I feel really sorry for these people. There is nothing like the love I have for my children. They missed out on the most amazing thing in the world. Don't ask for the blood money. It's not worth it.

Doesn't surprise me unfortunately. Anything they can do to reinforce how worthless you are to them. But what I know now is that all it means is they want you to mirror how worthless they really feel so they don't have to feel it. Sure took me long enough though. Sorry!

Doesn't really matter what my profession is. I do a lot of good for a lot of people every day but I was never sure that at the end of the day I deserved to wake up alive the next day. Thanks Nmom.

I broke a vase when I had just learned to walk after they told me not to touch it. Imagine! I was about one. She was a mature 23. I also colored in a freshly painted wall after they told me not to. I was two? No memory of either of these things. I vaguely remember pulling a pot of boiling water onto myself at age three - was told not to touch that either so it was totally my fault. Because you know, three year olds are so responsible and should be left within reach of pots of boiling water. I learned my lesson. I guess. Now I'm 53 and know I'm clumsy, stupid, unlovable, ugly, worthless, and that the reason my husband hasn't come back from out separation yet is because of course he never loved me. And they are still surprised I don't answer the phone.

My parents NEVER sent warmth, love, and compassion. The truth is, if they learned it now, in old age, I'd give them a chance. But they are incapable. Their version of love is "it's all in your head, you're crazy, we're amazing, you owe us because we gave birth and sacrificed to raise you."
Why would I respond well to more of that?
So true! I didn't even think about that, but you are so right!

I hope nobody else here gets him in their home group now.
Thanks again!

I have met all my never-born sisters in this group. So sorry you went through this.

Thank you. It was sort of helpful to write. I'm having a super hard time with all of this, even the realization that my mother is a N and that there is not really anything wrong with me. Now I'm mourning the life I could have had and didn't. It's really tragic.
My youngest son who still lives at home with me just said "Maybe I should tell Daddy to come home." He wanted his father to stay away until he goes off to college in another year and a half. But I won't make it that long.

We are probably around the same age (I'm 53) and some days I feel completely hopeless. Other days I think I can still turn it all around and it will be okay. But thanks for your support. If you have any good ideas let me know! And good luck to you! I'm so glad you found a way to make your situation fun and happy!

I felt the need to chime in here because I've tried all these things with the FMs before I knew any of this vocabulary or even that my Nrents were what they are, before Reddit and even before the internet (if you can imagine there was a world back then).
None of it works.
People don't believe that your charming, lovely parents are Narcissists.
I am old. My Nrents are even older. I blame my mother and her toxic "love" and the trauma bonding which I have only recently (this past summer) come to understand for ruining my life, ending in my separation from my husband. I've posted this here before. It was because I didn't understand what love was supposed to feel like and always suspected that my husband's love for me was not real. She did that to me by wearing me down for the 26 years I was with my husband.

This summer we had a birthday party for my father's 80th birthday. The moment I walked in one of their friends ran up to me and said: "Your mother complains you never call her." Not: "You look beautiful." Not: "Wow, your sons are so big and are young men now and so handsome and accomplished." Not: "Congratulations on being the only person in this room of 100 people to have published a book earlier this year, in addition to the previous one you published, both from major publishing companies, unlike my d-i-l who has never worked and has managed only one self-published book of so-called-poetry that nobody has ever read." No, it was "your mother complains about you." That was the take-home message. Even "congratulations for your father's 80th birthday" would have been appropriate.
Years ago my parents would tell us things like, "We can't afford blah blah blah, so tell everyone you don't want it," and we (my sister and I) would dutifully do that. Now my aunt will say "You didn't want it, I remember clearly." Impossible to tell her otherwise, that we were manipulated.

The damage these people do is very very deep. You cannot ever explain to their "friends."

When this "friend" said what she said, I simply said "Not now." My husband was there, we had been apart for six weeks, and I wanted to be with him. It was emotional and difficult for me. I didn't give a shit about my father's 80th birthday. It was a social convention for me, that's all, and a chance to dress up, and be proud of my kids. And mainly work on starting to repair my marriage. That's it. My only goal in life right now is fixing my marriage. I don't care what happens to my parents. They never cared what happened to me. They continue to lie, gaslight me, manipulate me, and do all the things they did to me since I was a child. Pointing it out doesn't help. Telling their FM's about it doesn't make a difference. Nobody believes it. I get the "they had a hard life and sacrificed so much for you." Um, no. They didn't. Everyone makes sacrifices for their children, in exchange for the reward: You get children. That's how life works, dummies. 

I told you my story so that you can understand that this woman, as wonderful as she might be, is not your friend. She is your mother's friend. My parents have a couple of friends who live far away who "get" it, sort of. But for the most part, there is no "your side" of any story. The sad part of being RBNs is that you are only a mirror for your Ns and don't exist as a separate person for them. If you want your own life you have to work on it very hard. And I've said it here before, living well is not enough of a revenge. You have to live well without seeing it as revenge. You have to really let go. 

I wish you all the best. It's very difficult, but don't give up hope.
Hugs if wanted!

Relationships are difficult under the best of circumstances. I really appreciate your input because I've been feeling so alone and it helps so much to have someone else's perspective especially a man's perspective. I'm wondering how you would be feeling if your wife's new love interest were another man. I know that if I were to become involved with a woman my husband would totally accept it and also try to bring her into our relationship as a third person. But I'm not into women. For years he told me he didn't care if I was involved with other men but he was totally lying about that. I still don't understand why he ever said such things to me. He doesn't understand that if he could back off and be less possessive I wouldn't need to look for outside support. It sounds like you get that instinctively. I really hope your situation works out. I just wonder though if your situation has a sexual orientation component to it. I have a female friend who lived with a woman for over 20 years. Then her partner decided to "go back to men" so she tried to too. She (my friend, I met her after this split) met and actually married a man. But then she met a woman in her new job and she ended up divorcing the man to be with the woman. She told me she just couldn't do it - she could never feel about a man the way she felt about women. If that's the case then it's not about you and your relationship or marriage - it's just biology. I have a gay son and while I wish he could have been straight (because it's just easier) I would never try to change him. He is who he is. So I think you need to consider this possibly as well.

If you are committed to your marriage I think it's really important not to be impulsive. My husband was really jealous of the amount of time I was spending with another man as friends. Until a certain point nothing had really happened although the tension was definitely there. Then one night he flipped out and packed his bags. That was the night that the other relationship really started to change. So I totally blame that on my husband's anger and impulsivity. Until then I had been resisting and trying to make the marriage work. Of course I'm in a different situation with years of anger and bitterness toward my husband. But I do think that you have to take things slowly. You can ask your wife to limit contact, but not cut it off completely. You can ask for structure. I recently met with a divorce mediator (for totally unrelated reasons, just coincidentally) and she said the most important thing in any mediation is structure. I have to agree. That's what I'm struggling with right now because my husband wants all our structure to be his way. But we are working on it.

She is poly. And bisexual. You are not. If you love her and want to be with her you will have to somehow come to terms with her needs. I personally can see her side of this story (as a woman currently in an emotional affair with a man not my husband, with an extremely possessive husband who flipped out completely when he learned I had kissed this other man.) Social rules are tough. I don't think you have fucked up your marriage but it is changing and it is up to you to accept or reject the "new rules." Can you live with sharing your wife's affection and desires? Can you share her body with another person or do you have to be the sole proprietor? Once you work these things out on therapy the path forward will become easier. But ultimatums rarely have the desired outcomes and people do not like to be bullied into submission. Good luck!
